title: 2027 budget approach and timeline
subtitle: Development charge pressures, reservist pension matching, prudent investor delegation, Q1 financial update and election compliance audit terms
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that Council direct staff to present the 2027 Plan and Budget timetable to the incoming Regional Chair {{vote:m6}}. Staff outlined a preliminary 2027 operating pressure of about 6.1 per cent, excluding police, which they described as the cost of keeping existing services in place. Timeline options reflect uncertainty about the Region's governance model after the election.

The committee also recommended adopting a by-law so the Region can match OMERS contributions for employees on reservist leave {{vote:m4}}. It recommended a by-law delegating authority to the outgoing council to consider adopting the prudent investor standard for investments {{vote:m5}}. Through the consent agenda, it recommended revised Municipal Election Compliance Audit Committee terms of reference and an amended 2026 capital budget alongside the first-quarter update.

Councillors received a report on development charges for information. It described falling revenue from exemptions and deferrals, and a new provincial and federal program that requires reduced charges. The June 19 application deadline is close, and the cost to taxpayers is unclear. A closed session followed; the minutes report only its listed subjects.

decisions.item: 2027 Plan and Budget approach and timeline
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff present the 2027 Plan and Budget timetable to the incoming Regional Chair, as set out in Appendix A.
The committee recommended adopting a by-law allowing the Region to match OMERS contributions for employees buying back service broken by approved reservist leave.
The committee recommended a by-law delegating authority to the outgoing council to pass by-laws authorizing potential adoption of the prudent investor standard.
The committee recommended receiving the first quarter update and amending the 2026 Capital Budget as set out in Appendix B.
The committee recommended approving the revised Municipal Election Compliance Audit Committee Terms of Reference for 2026-2030.

debate: On development charges, several councillors said the Region has kept its charges low and could be left out or not rewarded under the new program, which requires reduced charges and a municipal share of at least 10 per cent. Staff said analysis was only starting and debt was the likely way to fund the municipal share.

Councillors raised concern that the cost could fall on taxpayers through the levy or water rates. One asked staff to report a worst-case scenario. Staff said regional and municipal officials had raised fairness concerns with the province, and that the short deadline for naming projects was a challenge.

On the 2027 budget, one councillor urged scenarios at inflation and inflation plus one per cent, and a four-year rotating departmental review. Staff said inflation alone would likely mean service reductions, and transit could face a cut of several million dollars.

Councillors asked whether police could be given a budget target. Staff said they could work with the police service but could not direct a figure. The clerk noted that any target would not bind the next council.
Other requests included household ability-to-pay analysis, a possible auditor general function, and details on water reserve spending ahead of the July water financial update.
